decisions.reason: Weekly reassessment of the session SDK Dynamic Workflows doc (fetched 2026-11-07). The source hash changed since 2026-10-31. It still says the API is experimental and execution needs eligible credentials. Cost limits are soft. No human date or gate is renewed. This is not GitHub Agentic Workflows (Actions).

citations.quote: Dynamic Workflows are extension-authored, session-scoped workflows that coordinate subagents and durable steps. The API is experimental.
still require eligible credentials (token-based billing or trusted HMAC authentication).
This is a soft, post-paid ceiling, so completed or parallel turns can settle above it before the run stops.
Workflow-owned subagents are intentionally hidden from read_agent

findings.reason: Doc says the API is experimental and execution needs token-based billing or trusted HMAC authentication. Ineligible requests fail with dynamic_workflows_unavailable. Tenant and plan eligibility are not documented here.
findings.next: Confirm eligibility with a named pilot identity and an ineligible control identity.

findings.reason: The doc names no enterprise policy or setting to disable or restrict Dynamic Workflows.
findings.next: Find an official admin control and run a negative enforcement test.

findings.reason: Only credential eligibility is described. How workflow subagents map to the user identity and permissions is not documented here.
findings.next: Verify the identity and permissions subagents run under in a test session.

findings.reason: Runs are journaled in session workflow storage, which needs SQLite support. Retention, residency and prompt content handling are not stated.
findings.next: Document where journals live, their retention, and what they contain.

findings.reason: ctx.pause gives a durable checkpoint. The doc says SDK-initiated run and resume request no permission, so approval must be built into the workflow.
findings.next: Test a pause checkpoint and confirm no run starts without explicit approval.

findings.reason: Run, progress and detail APIs exist. Workflow-owned subagents are hidden from read_agent. Export, retention and tamper resistance are not documented.
findings.next: Check whether run history can be exported and retained for audit.

findings.reason: maxAiCredits is a soft, post-paid ceiling and turns can settle above it. Billed-spend behavior is unmeasured.
findings.next: Measure credits for a synthetic run and set a separate billing budget.

findings.reason: The doc does not describe network destinations or proxy and firewall behavior for workflow subagents.
findings.next: Capture network behavior in a controlled test session.

findings.reason: Pause, resume, cancel and limit failures are documented. Support ownership, monitoring and the experimental-API change policy are not.
findings.next: Name an owner and a change-watch process for SDK doc updates.

findings.reason: Runs can be cancelled. The doc does not describe undoing side effects from workflow subagents or disabling the feature fleet-wide.
findings.next: Define cancel and cleanup steps for synthetic runs and test them.
